result.summary: This PR revives two test-only commits from a 2022 PR (#24361), adapting them to the current descriptor_tests.cpp DoCheck() signature. It adds a DropKeys()-based roundtrip check (inferring a descriptor from its generated script and comparing structure, with special handling for MuSig and BIP389 multipath key expressions and taproot sibling ordering), and adds Check() coverage for valid raw()/addr() descriptors via a new NO_KEYS flag, previously only exercised as invalid inputs.
result.problem: The descriptor test suite lacked roundtrip verification (infer-from-script back to original structure) and lacked positive-path coverage for raw()/addr() descriptors, which are exercised only in negative tests today; this leaves gaps a maintainer relying on these tests for confidence would want closed.

categories.evidence: PR is entirely within src/test/descriptor_tests.cpp, adding test-only coverage with no production code change, matching the Tests label and the tests category's coverage-of-high-risk-paths criterion.
categories.rationale: P3 because it closes real coverage gaps (roundtrip inference and raw()/addr() positive-path checks) in a security-adjacent area (descriptor parsing) with no behavior change and no urgency. jeanpablojp's mutation-testing evidence shows the new tests do catch failures (60 failures under a tested InferScript mutation) but also that some claimed coverage (ToPrivateString for NO_KEYS, sortedmulti_a) is incomplete, which is exactly the kind of gap this category values fixing but is not itself high severity since descriptor parsing already has extensive existing coverage.

result.card: This PR revives two orphaned test-only commits from a 2022 PR (#24361), adding descriptor roundtrip verification (infer-from-script back to structure) and Check() coverage for valid raw()/addr() descriptors in src/test/descriptor_tests.cpp, with no production code change. It closes real gaps in descriptor test coverage, an area adjacent to consensus-relevant parsing code, though the change itself carries no urgency since existing coverage is already extensive. Two concept ACKs were given (w0xlt, jeanpablojp), but jeanpablojp's 2026-09-03 review, backed by mutation-testing evidence, raised three specific unresolved questions about gaps in the new tests (an avoidable comparison, a missed sortedmulti_a regex case, and an unasserted ToPrivateString contract for keyless descriptors), and the author has not replied in over two weeks. No dependencies block this PR, though the author notes a follow-up Part 2 (ToString/ToPrivateString merge) needs more design work first.
